p.src: Now Jin Rong, outnumbered and overpowered, and moreover compelled by Jia Rui, admitted that he was in the wrong and kowtowed to Qin Zhong; only then did Baoyu cease making a disturbance. When school was dismissed and everyone had gone, Jin Rong returned home and grew angrier the more he thought about it. “Qin Zhong is merely Jia Rong's brother-in-law,” he said. “He isn't even a descendant of the Jia family. He attends their school as an affiliate, no differently from me. Because he relies on Baoyu's affection for him, he treats everyone else as beneath his notice. If that is how he means to behave, he ought at least to conduct himself properly, and then no one would have anything to say. Yet he is forever skulking about with Baoyu, as though everyone else were blind and could see nothing. Today he tried to make advances to someone else, and I happened to catch him at it with my own eyes. Even if it causes an uproar, what have I to fear?”

p.src: His mother, née Hu, heard him muttering and grumbling, and asked, “What pointless quarrel are you trying to start now? It was hard enough for me to appeal to your aunt, and only after she tried every possible means and spoke to Second Mistress Lian at the Western Mansion did you obtain this place to study. If we could not depend on them, would our family have the means to hire a tutor? Besides, tea and meals are both provided at their school. During the two years you have studied there, our household has saved a great deal on food and other daily expenses. And with what we save, you are able to indulge your taste for bright new clothes. What is more, if you had not been studying there, would you ever have become acquainted with Master Xue? Master Xue gives us something every year, and in these last two years he has helped our family to the amount of seventy or eighty taels of silver. If you now make such trouble that you are thrown out of this school, let me tell you, finding another place like it will be harder than climbing to heaven! Now be good, amuse yourself quietly for a while, and then go to sleep. That will be far better.” Thus Jin Rong swallowed his anger and said no more; before long he went off to bed. The next day he went to school as usual. There is no more to be said of that.

p.src: Now his aunt had originally been betrothed to a direct descendant of the Jia family's jade-name generation, a man called Jia Huang. It goes without saying that not every member of the clan could equal the wealth and power of the Ning and Rong Mansions. Jia Huang and his wife lived on a small property. They frequently went to pay their respects at the Ning and Rong Mansions and knew how to ingratiate themselves with Xifeng and Lady You; consequently, Xifeng and Lady You often gave them assistance, and only thus were they able to make ends meet. That day the weather happened to be fine and she had nothing to occupy her at home, so she took an old maidservant with her, boarded her carriage, and went to visit her widowed sister-in-law and nephew.

p.src: In the course of their casual conversation, Jin Rong's mother happened to bring up the previous day's affair at the Jia family school and related every detail from beginning to end to her sister-in-law. The moment Mistress Huang heard it, anger flared in her heart. “That little wretch Qin Zhong is a relative of the Jia family,” she cried, “but isn't our Rong a relative of theirs too? People ought not to be so abominably snobbish—especially when none of them was engaged in anything honorable! Even Baoyu had no call to take his side to such an extent. Wait until I go to the Eastern Mansion to see our Mistress Zhen. I shall speak to Qin Zhong's sister as well and ask her to judge who is in the right.” Jin Rong's mother was terribly alarmed when she heard this and hurriedly said, “It was all because I spoke too freely and told you about it, Auntie. Please don't go, and never mind who was right or wrong. If it causes an uproar, how could he remain at the school? If he cannot remain there, not only can our family not afford to hire a tutor, but we shall also have to bear many more expenses for him.” Mistress Huang replied, “I don't care about any of that. Just wait until I have had my say, and we shall see what happens!” Without allowing her sister-in-law to dissuade her, she ordered the old maidservant to see to the carriage, climbed aboard, and set off for the Ning Mansion.

p.src: Upon reaching the Ning Mansion, she entered through the carriage gate, alighted before the small eastern side gate, and went in to see You-shi, Jia Zhen’s wife. She no longer dared assume an overbearing air, but exchanged warm and attentive greetings and made some small talk before asking, “Why have I not seen young Mistress Rong today?” You-shi replied, “For some reason, she has not had her monthly courses for more than two months. We had a physician examine her, but he said it was not pregnancy. Over the last couple of days, by afternoon she has been too listless to move or even speak, and her eyes grow dizzy. I told her, ‘You need not stand on ceremony for now. You need not come up morning and evening as usual; just rest and take good care of yourself. Even if relatives from any branch of the family come, I shall be here to receive them. And if any of the elders blame you, I shall explain matters on your behalf.’ I even cautioned Brother Rong, saying, ‘You are not to wear her out or provoke her; let her rest quietly and she will recover. Whatever she wishes to eat, simply come and fetch it from me. If I do not have it here, just ask your second aunt Lian for it. If anything should happen to her, you could search by lantern-light and still never find another wife with such beauty and such a nature.’ With the way she conducts herself, what relative or elder in the family does not love her? That is why I have been so troubled these past two days that worry is consuming me. And as ill luck would have it, her brother came to see her this morning. The foolish child saw that his sister was unwell, yet failed to understand that even if something had happened he ought not tell her. Let alone such a trifling matter—even if he had suffered the gravest injustice, he still should not have spoken of it to her. It seems they had a fight in the schoolroom yesterday, and someone who had joined the school from elsewhere had bullied him. There was also some indecent talk involved, and he told his sister all of it. Aunt, you know what that daughter-in-law of mine is like: though she smiles and converses readily with others and always behaves properly, she is sensitive and takes things deeply to heart. Whatever she hears, she will brood over it for three days and five nights before letting it rest. Her illness has arisen from the brooding caused by that very disposition. When she heard today that someone had bullied her brother, she was both incensed and angry. She was incensed at those wretched scoundrels and disreputable companions who spread tales, stirred up trouble, and sowed discord; and angry that her brother would not behave himself or apply his mind to his studies, thereby causing such an uproar at school. After hearing of it, she would not even eat breakfast today. When I heard, I went to her rooms and comforted her for a while, then spent some time admonishing and soothing her brother.

Aunt, tell me—how could I not be frantic with worry? Besides, there is no good physician to be found nowadays. Whenever I think of her illness, it feels as though needles were piercing my heart. Do you happen to know of any good physician?”

p.src: After listening to this long account, Madam Jin’s earlier burst of righteous fury at her sister-in-law’s house, with which she had meant to confront Qin-shi, had long since been frightened clean away to the ends of the earth. Hearing You-shi ask whether she knew of a good physician, she hastily replied, “From all that we hear, we truly have never heard anyone mention a good physician. From what you have just said about young Mistress Rong, though, it may yet turn out to be pregnancy. You had better not let just anyone treat her indiscriminately. If they mistake the condition, the consequences could be dreadful.” “Precisely,” said You-shi. As they were speaking, Jia Zhen entered from outside. Seeing Madam Jin, he asked You-shi, “Is that not young Mistress Huang?” Madam Jin stepped forward and paid her respects to Jia Zhen. Jia Zhen said to You-shi, “See that our young cousin stays for a meal before she leaves.” With that, Jia Zhen went into the adjoining room. Madam Jin had originally come to speak to Qin-shi about Qin Zhong bullying her nephew; but on hearing that Qin-shi was ill, she not only could not discuss it, she no longer dared even mention it. Moreover, Jia Zhen and You-shi treated her with such kindness that her anger turned to delight. After chatting for a while longer, she finally went home.

p.src: After Madam Jin had left, Jia Zhen came over and sat down. He asked Madam You, “What did she come to discuss today?” Madam You replied, “Nothing in particular. When she first came in, she looked rather angry, but after talking for some time and then mentioning our daughter-in-law’s illness, her expression gradually settled down. You also invited her to stay for a meal, but when she heard how ill our daughter-in-law was, she felt it improper to linger. After a little more idle talk, she left without asking for anything. For now, we must attend to our daughter-in-law’s illness. The important thing is for you to find a good physician to examine her; we must not let it drag on. The physicians who currently attend our household are no good at all. Every one of them merely takes his cue from what people say, then repeats it with a few learned phrases added. They are certainly diligent enough: three or four of them take turns coming four or five times a day to feel her pulse. They confer among themselves and write a prescription, yet the medicine has no effect. Instead, they make her change clothes four or five times a day and sit up to receive them, which in truth does the patient no good at all.” Jia Zhen said, “Quite so. The child is foolish too. Why must she keep undressing and changing? If she catches another chill and adds a fresh illness to the first, what then? However fine the clothes may be, what are they worth compared with the child’s health? Even if she wore a new outfit every day, the cost would be nothing. Indeed, I came in expressly to tell you this: Feng Ziying called on me just now. Seeing that I looked troubled, he asked what was wrong. I told him that our daughter-in-law had suddenly become seriously unwell, and because we could find no good imperial physician, no one could determine whether she was with child or ill, nor whether the condition was dangerous. That is why I have been truly anxious these past two days. Feng Ziying then spoke of a former tutor of his from childhood, whose surname is Zhang and personal name Youshi. He is a man of the most profound learning, possesses exceptionally deep medical knowledge, and can even judge whether a patient will live or die. He came to the capital this year to purchase an official post for his son and is now staying at Feng’s house. It may be that fate has ordained this man to deliver our daughter-in-law from her affliction. I immediately sent a servant with my card to invite him. If it is too late for him to come today, he will surely come tomorrow. Besides, Feng Ziying went straight home to entreat him in person and make certain that he comes to examine her. Let us wait until this Mr. Zhang has examined her before deciding what to do.”

p.src: Madam You was delighted to hear this and said, “The day after tomorrow is the Old Master’s birthday. What, in the end, are we to do?” Jia Zhen replied, “I went to pay my respects to the Old Master just now and also invited him to come home and receive the family’s homage. But the Old Master said, ‘I am accustomed to peace and quiet. I have no wish to go and join the commotion in that arena of disputes of yours. You will surely say that because it is my birthday I must go and receive everyone’s kowtows. Far better—indeed, a hundred times better than making me accept their bows for no good reason—would be for you to have my former commentary on the Treatise on Hidden Virtue carefully copied out and printed. If members of the family come during those two days, simply entertain them properly at home. There is no need to send me any gifts, and you need not come the day after tomorrow either. If your conscience troubles you, kowtow to me today and be done with it. If you do come the day after tomorrow with a crowd of followers to disturb me, I shall hold you to account.’ He repeated this again and again, so I certainly dare not go the day after tomorrow. For now, summon Lai Sheng and instruct him to prepare banquets for two days.” Madam You therefore sent for Jia Rong and told him, “Instruct Lai Sheng to prepare two days of banquets according to the customary arrangements, and make them especially lavish. Then go personally to the Western Mansion and invite the Old Lady, the First Lady, the Second Lady, and your Second Aunt Lian to come and enjoy themselves. Today your father also heard of an excellent physician and has already sent someone to invite him. He will surely come tomorrow. You must explain to him in detail all the symptoms she has shown over these past days.”

p.src: Jia Rong acknowledged each instruction and went out. Just then he encountered the servant who had been sent to Feng Ziying’s house to invite the physician. The servant reported, “I went to Master Feng’s house just now and presented the master’s card to invite the gentleman here. The gentleman said, ‘The young master here spoke to me about it a short while ago. But I have spent the whole day making calls and have only just returned home. At present I am truly too exhausted; even if I went to your mansion, I would not be able to take the patient’s pulse.’ He said that after resting for the night, he would without fail come to the mansion tomorrow. He also said, ‘My medical knowledge is shallow, and I would ordinarily never dare accept so weighty a recommendation. But since both your Master Feng and the lord of your mansion have spoken in this manner, I cannot refuse to go. Please report this to his lordship on my behalf. I am truly unworthy of receiving his lordship’s card.’ And so he made me bring the card back. Young master, please report this for me.” Jia Rong turned and went back inside. After reporting the servant’s words to Jia Zhen and Madam You, he came out again, summoned Lai Sheng, and instructed him to prepare banquets for two days. Having heard the instructions, Lai Sheng went off to make the customary arrangements. There is no need to say more of this.

p.src: At noon the next day, a servant came to report, “The physician Mr. Zhang whom we invited has arrived.” Jia Zhen thereupon ushered him into the main hall and invited him to sit. When they had finished their tea, Jia Zhen began, “Yesterday, Master Feng told me of your character and learning, sir, and of your profound knowledge of medicine as well. I cannot adequately express my admiration.” Mr. Zhang replied, “I am merely an uncultivated and insignificant scholar of shallow knowledge. Yesterday Master Feng told me that Your Lordship’s noble household treats humble scholars with courtesy, and since I was also honored with a summons, how could I dare disobey? Yet having no true learning at all, I can only blush all the more deeply.” Jia Zhen said, “There is no need for such modesty, sir. Please go in and examine my daughter-in-law. I rely upon your skill to relieve my anxiety.” Jia Rong then accompanied him inside. When they reached Jia Rong’s apartments and he saw Lady Qin, the physician asked Jia Rong, “Is this your wife?” “She is,” replied Jia Rong. Please be seated, sir. Shall I first tell you about my wife’s illness, and then have you take her pulse?” The physician replied, “In my humble opinion, it would be better to take her pulse before we discuss anything. This is my first visit to your honored residence, so naturally I know nothing of the case. But Master Feng insisted that I come and examine her, and thus I could not decline. Once I have taken her pulse, we can see whether my conclusions are correct. Then you may tell me how the illness has progressed over these past days, and together we can consider a prescription and whether it is suitable. The final decision will then rest with you, sir.” Jia Rong said, “Your method truly shows great wisdom. I only regret that we did not meet sooner. Please take her pulse and tell us whether she can be cured, so that my parents may set their minds at ease.” The young married servants of the household brought over a large pulse-taking cushion, while one of them drew back Lady Qin’s cuff to expose her wrist. Only then did the physician place his fingers upon the pulse of her right wrist. Regulating his breathing, he counted the beats and examined it with full concentration for about a quarter of an hour; then he changed to the left wrist and proceeded in the same manner. After completing the examination, he said, “Let us sit in the outer room.”

Jia Zhen said, “There is no need for such modesty, sir.
Please go in and examine my daughter-in-law. I rely upon your skill to relieve my anxiety.”
Jia Rong then accompanied him inside.
When they reached Jia Rong’s apartments and he saw Lady Qin, the physician asked Jia Rong, “Is this your wife?”
“She is,” replied Jia Rong.
Please be seated, sir. Shall I first tell you about my wife’s illness, and then have you take her pulse?”
The physician replied, “In my humble opinion, it would be better to take her pulse before we discuss anything.
This is my first visit to your honored residence, so naturally I know nothing of the case. But Master Feng insisted that I come and examine her, and thus I could not decline.

Once I have taken her pulse, we can see whether my conclusions are correct. Then you may tell me how the illness has progressed over these past days, and together we can consider a prescription and whether it is suitable. The final decision will then rest with you, sir.”
Jia Rong said, “Your method truly shows great wisdom. I only regret that we did not meet sooner.
Please take her pulse and tell us whether she can be cured, so that my parents may set their minds at ease.”
The young married servants of the household brought over a large pulse-taking cushion, while one of them drew back Lady Qin’s cuff to expose her wrist.

Only then did the physician place his fingers upon the pulse of her right wrist. Regulating his breathing, he counted the beats and examined it with full concentration for about a quarter of an hour; then he changed to the left wrist and proceeded in the same manner.
After completing the examination, he said, “Let us sit in the outer room.”

p.src: Jia Rong accompanied the physician into the outer room, where they sat on the kang; an old serving woman brought them tea. “Please have some tea, sir,” said Jia Rong. After keeping the physician company over tea, he asked, “Judging from her pulse, sir, can she still be cured or not?” The physician replied, “Your wife’s pulse presents as follows: the left cun position is deep and rapid, the left guan position deep and hidden; the right cun position is fine and weak, while the right guan position is deficient and without vitality. The deep and rapid pulse at the left cun means that weakness of the heart qi has given rise to internal heat; the deep and hidden pulse at the left guan means stagnation of liver qi and deficiency of blood. The fine and weak pulse at the right cun signifies an extreme deficiency of qi in the lung channel; the deficient and lifeless pulse at the right guan means that the spleen, which belongs to earth, is being overpowered by the liver, which belongs to wood. When weakness of the heart qi gives rise to heat, the symptoms should include irregular menstruation and sleeplessness at night. When the liver is deficient in blood and its qi is stagnant, there must be pain and distension beneath the ribs, delayed menstruation, and a sensation of heat within. When the qi of the lung channel is severely deficient, the head and eyes are often dizzy, and between the hours of the tiger and the hare she must break into spontaneous perspiration and feel as though she were sitting in a boat. When the spleen-earth is overpowered by the liver-wood, she must have no desire for food, feel weary and listless, and suffer aching weakness in all four limbs. From my reading of her pulse, these should indeed be her symptoms. If anyone takes this pulse for the pulse of pregnancy, I cannot agree with his instruction.” An old woman who waited personally upon Lady Qin said from beside them, “Why, that is exactly how it is! Your diagnosis is truly miraculous, sir; there was no need for us to tell you anything. Several imperial physicians are treating her in our household even now, yet not one of them has been able to speak with such accuracy and certainty. One says she is pregnant, another that she is ill; one says it is nothing serious, while another fears she may not survive the winter solstice. None of them gives us a definite answer. Please, sir, give us a clear and definite judgment.”

p.src: The physician smiled. “The young mistress’s condition has indeed been allowed to worsen through the delay of those other doctors. Had medicine been administered from the time of her first irregular menstruation, not only would she certainly have escaped her present affliction, but by now she would have recovered completely. Now that the illness has been neglected until it has reached this stage, however, this calamity was bound to befall her. As I see it, there are still three chances in ten of curing her. Let us see how she fares after taking my medicine. If she can sleep at night, I shall have two more chances in ten of mastering the illness. From her pulse, I can tell that the young mistress is a woman of proud and determined temperament and exceptional intelligence. But excessive intelligence makes disappointments frequent, and frequent disappointments lead to excessive brooding. This illness arose because anxiety injured the spleen and the liver-wood became excessively vigorous; consequently, her menstrual blood could not arrive at the proper time. Ask about the dates of the young mistress’s former periods: they were certainly never habitually early, but must often have been late. Is that not so?” The old woman replied, “Indeed it is. Her periods have never once come early. Sometimes they were two or three days late, and sometimes as many as ten.” On hearing this, the physician said, “Excellent! That is the very root of the illness. Had she formerly taken medicine to nourish the heart and regulate menstruation, how could matters ever have come to this? She now clearly manifests a condition in which water is deficient and wood overabundant. Let us try medicine and observe the result.” He then wrote out a prescription and handed it to Jia Rong. p.src: Jia Rong looked it over and said, “It is remarkably insightful. May I ask you one more thing, sir: will this illness ultimately endanger her life or not?” The physician smiled. “You, sir, are the truly perceptive one. For an illness to reach this stage is not the work of a day or two. Even after she takes this medicine, the outcome will depend on whether fate favors the physician’s efforts. In my judgment, she should come to no harm throughout this winter. If she makes it past the spring equinox, there will be hope of a complete recovery.” Jia Rong was an intelligent man himself and did not press him for further details. Jia Rong then saw the physician out. Only afterward did he show both the prescription and the written pulse diagnosis to Jia Zhen, repeating everything the physician had said to Jia Zhen and Lady You. Lady You said to Jia Zhen, “No physician has ever spoken as plainly as he did. I expect his medicine will be sound as well.” Jia Zhen replied, “He is not one of those habitual physicians who practice merely to earn their keep. It was only because we are close to Feng Ziying that he managed, with great difficulty, to persuade him to come. Now that we have such a man, perhaps our daughter-in-law’s illness really can be cured. His prescription calls for ginseng, so use the good catty we bought the other day.” After hearing this, Jia Rong went out and ordered someone to obtain the medicines, decoct them, and give the draught to Lady Qin. How Lady Qin’s condition fared after taking this medicine will be revealed in the next chapter.
